title: Trust Accounting Memo: The Amount a Per-Bill Ancillary Authorization Covers
content:
A per-bill authorization on a Resident Trust Fund Accounts account for an ancillary charge names the most recent one-time item charge on the resident's Ancillary and Optional Services Billing account (of two on the same date, the one recorded first). The amount it covers is figured as follows.

## 1. The amount

The amount a new per-bill authorization covers is the lesser of the named charge's open balance and the account's spare balance, never below zero, rounded half up to the cent once, on the final amount only. The named charge's open balance is the charge less the payments and credits naming it.

## 2. The spare balance

The spare balance is the account balance (the deposits, interest credits and returns on the account's ledger less its withdrawals, bill transfers and conveyances), less every deposit whose available date is after today, because a transfer never exceeds the available balance and a check deposit still on hold is not available; less the personal needs allowance of the resident's Medical Assistance case where the account is in the Resident Funds Account, Medicaid Representative Payee tier, because for a Medicaid payee account the personal needs allowance stays in the account; less the coinsurance run-up; and less the held-bed charges building up.

## 3. The coinsurance run-up

The coinsurance run-up is the resident's share of the coinsurance on the coinsurance days of the run of the active episode under Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage: each such day at the daily coinsurance rate due for it times the share percent that applies to it, over one hundred. With no active Part A episode there is no run and no run-up.

- **The run** is the days of the active Part A episode from the run's first day through the run's end. The run starts on the episode's coverage start date and ends yesterday, every day of the episode from that date counted in it.
- **Numbering.** For the reserve the run's days are numbered in turn in the benefit period from the days the coverage office has booked: the first day of the run is the SNF days already used in the benefit period before the episode, plus the net covered days booked in the episode before the run's first day (days booked less days reversed), plus one. Only the days numbered above the episode's full-coverage day limit and not above its benefit-period day limit are coinsurance days.
- **Rate.** The daily coinsurance rate due for a run day is the rate of the calendar year the day falls in: a day in 2026 takes the 2026 rate, $217.00; a day in 2025 takes the 2025 rate, $209.50; a day in any other year takes the rate of the episode's most recent coinsurance charge.
- **Share percent.** The share the supplemental coverage on the episode sets applies to the coinsurance days from the date that coverage took effect: where it took effect on or before the run's first day, every coinsurance day of the run; where it took effect after the run's first day, the run's coinsurance days from that date, the earlier ones keeping the whole coinsurance, because days before the supplemental effective date keep the earlier split; where no supplemental effective date is recorded, none, every coinsurance day keeping the whole coinsurance. The share the supplemental coverage sets is the whole coinsurance, 100 percent.
- **Nights away.** The run-up is a reserve for what the run will cost the resident: every day of the run is reserved as a day in the center, a night away included, because a night away during a Part A stay is billed instead as a held night at the private rate of the room held, which is never less than the coinsurance reserved for it.

## 4. The held-bed charges building up

These come from the hold in progress under Bed-Hold and Leave Reservations. The held nights follow the hold: a private-pay or Medicare skilled-stay hold builds up its nights so far not yet charged; a Medicaid hospital-leave reserved bed builds up only its nights so far beyond the reserved nights per hospitalization not yet charged; any other case, including no hold in progress, builds up no night.

- A held night is reserved at the full bed-hold rate, the most a held night can bill, because an extended-hold percent or a dietary credit that a bed-hold charge agreement applies once the leave has ended depends on the leave's final length.
- The hold's nights so far are the nights from the leave start date through yesterday. The nights already charged on the reservation, and for a reserved bed the reserved nights before them, are the earliest of those nights.
- Nights build up from the first night allowed, which is the hold's first held day: the private hold start date the reservation records, or its leave start date where it records none.
- Each night is at the bed-hold rate of the room tier priced in effect that night: the schedule taking effect 2026-07-01 for nights from that date, and the schedule taking effect 2025-07-01 for earlier nights. The room tier priced is the room tier of the resident's Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency agreement; where no room tier is recorded, no night is priced.

| Room tier | Schedule taking effect 2025-07-01 | Schedule taking effect 2026-07-01 |
|---|---|---|
| Semi-Private Long-Term Care Room | $384.00 a night | $398.00 a night |
| Semi-Private Secure Memory Care Room | $412.00 a night | $427.00 a night |
| Private Long-Term Care Room | $421.00 a night | $436.00 a night |
| Private Secure Memory Care Room | $449.00 a night | $465.00 a night |
| Private Bariatric Care Room | $466.00 a night | $482.00 a night |
| Private Suite with Sitting Area | $497.00 a night | $514.00 a night |## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

Today is 11 February 2026. A Non-Medicaid Self-Directed account shows a balance of $2406.85 and no deposit before its available date. The resident's active Part A episode began on 3 February 2026, after 31 SNF days already used in the benefit period; no supplemental effective date is recorded. No hold is in progress.

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| run: 3 to 10 February, numbered 32 to 39, all coinsurance days | 8 days |
| coinsurance run-up: 8 days at the 2026 rate of $217.00 at 100 percent | $1736.00 |
| spare balance: $2406.85 less $1736.00 | $670.85 |
| named one-time charge, open balance | $940.00 |
| amount covered: the lesser of $940.00 and $670.85 | **$670.85** |

Had the named charge's open balance been $64.85, the amount covered would be $64.85.
